title: Ant-mediated ecosystem services and disservices on marketable yield in cocoa agroforestry systems
authors: Bisseleua DHB, Begoude D, Tonnang H, Vidal S
location: Central Cameroon (5 sites: Boumnyebel, Obala, Talba, Bakoa, Kedia), 4°12'–4°30'N, 10°6'–11°15'E
design: 20 cocoa plots (30x30m) each with 6 subplots (10x10m, 10 trees each). Treatments randomly assigned: (i) non-manipulated control, (ii) Crematogaster sp. only, (iii) O. longinoda only, (iv) Crematogaster+C. brutus, (v) O. longinoda+C. brutus, (vi) ant exclusion via nest destruction and insect glue barriers. 18-month experiment Jan 2012–Jul 2013. Linear mixed-effects models with plot as random effect. Cultivars SNK 16 and T79/467.
notes: 20 plots each contain one subplot per treatment giving 20 replicates per treatment. However ANOVA df (F5,23) suggest effective replication may be lower due to mixed model structure. Yield data from first 12 months. All yield values from Fig. 4; percentage differences stated in text. Error bars in figures are +/- SE. Ant exclusion reduced ant worker abundance by >87%. The eligible PICO comparison is ant exclusion vs non-manipulated control. Single-species dominance treatments represent ant community manipulation rather than simple exclusion/addition but are also recorded for completeness.

Text confirms '34% lower in ant exclusion treatments' which is consistent: (2000-3000)/3000 = -33.3%, close to 34%. SEM estimated ~200 from error bar cap.

observations.tissue: pods lost to P. megakarya (pod rot disease)

figure_read.structure: Three groups: P. megakarya, S. singularis, C. stictigrapta. 6 bars per group (same legend as Fig 2). Y-axis 'Number of pods' 0-300, ticks at 50 intervals. +/-SE error bars.
figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 3 p5; P. megakarya group; bars are very small and crowded for ant exclusion and control treatments making precise reads impossible. Text states: 'Ant exclusion resulted in significantly less infections on pods compared to the control (t=9.5; p<0.0001)'. Direction is OPPOSITE to pest abundance — excluding ants REDUCES disease because ants vector fungal spores. This is a disservice of ants, not biocontrol.

observations.notes: Ant exclusion REDUCES P. megakarya disease because ants vector the fungal pathogen — this is an ant disservice, not a biocontrol failure. Precise values not readable from Fig 3 due to crowded bars. Text confirms direction: ant exclusion = significantly fewer infected pods than control.

observations.tissue: pods lost to S. singularis (mirid pest)

figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 3 p5; S. singularis group; ant exclusion bar appears highest among all treatments at ~60-70 pods; control bar appears at ~10-15 pods. Text: 'total pods lost due to S. singularis was highest in ant exclusion subplots' (F5,23=7.3; p<0.001). Direction as expected: excluding predatory ants increases pest damage.

observations.notes: S. singularis damage highest in ant exclusion — expected direction (removing ant predators increases pest damage). Precise bar values too crowded to digitize reliably from Fig 3.
